gop_handoff.appleclcd_provider_contract: AppleCLCD matches IONameMatch disp0,t8010 | disp0,t8011 under IOProviderClass AppleARMIODevice; backlight-control property match; display timing data is expected from the DT platform device, not from a GOP handle
gop_handoff.conclusion: a stock kernelcache exposes no GOP/UEFI framebuffer hand-off object; the shipped display stack is a DT AppleARMIODevice/AppleCLCD graph. A Polar GOP-owned nub plus its ownership hand-off cannot be qualified from these bytes and requires board-side evidence.

iosurface_accessors.semantics: pinned Sirius accessor names plus independently matched local load/return instructions; kernel-only stable IOSurface input required

module_delta_analysis.conclusion: family-owned slots share one module-relative delta; kernel-owned slots do not share a single slide and are individually resolvable through the local kernel export symbol table

missing_evidence: No exported kext symbols: per-slot prototype names and demangled signatures cannot be recovered from this stock image.
Constructor/destructor bodies are located structurally (vtable materialization, super-call chain) but their source-level prototypes and member layouts are not proven.
IOSurface accessor names come from the pinned public reference; descriptor ownership, pixel-format values and CPU-completion semantics are not provable from local instruction bytes.
Swap pending/current lock, retention and completion state machine is not established; hypothesis field offsets are only partially consistent with local encodings.
Stock prelinked import tables are already bound; there is no relocation/import descriptor for a late-loaded adapter. A new adapter must obtain its bindings from the same prelink/kxld pipeline.
GOP ownership hand-off and the producer call into polaris_display_present have no stock-kernelcache evidence; the shipped provider graph is DT AppleARMIODevice/AppleCLCD.
No runtime, hardware, panel, backlight or vblank evidence exists in this report.
